meta.comment: engine.traffic (planned MOD) inc0 table (a): mode-share by density band and trip purpose. This is the SOURCE table scale_ladder.json's per-rung modeShare rows are log-linearly interpolated from (see traffic-assumptions.md A-4..A-6 for the interpolation rule). Mode ids match data/modes.json's 12 mode ids exactly except hs_rail, which is this schema's own id for the high-speed-rail sub-market of data/modes.json's heavy_rail mode (heavy_rail carries both conventional and HS1-class services in modes.json; this table splits them because their density-band shares diverge sharply at megacity scale). Every band's 11-way (12 counting the hs_rail split) share vector sums to 1.0 exactly.
meta.unitsConvention: densityPersonsPerKm2 in persons/km2 (band lower threshold, inclusive); shares are dimensionless fractions of daily person-trips, summing to 1.0 per band per purpose-less (all-purpose) split. A future increment may add a purpose dimension (commute/education/shopping/leisure/business) sourced from NTS0409's purpose breakdown -- deferred, noted as A-7 in traffic-assumptions.md; this v1 table is all-purpose only, matching what scale_ladder.json currently consumes.

provenance.source: Composite: UK DfT National Travel Survey (NTS -- mode share by settlement type, rural/small-town/urban bands), Tokyo Metropolitan Area Person Trip Survey (5th round, MLIT/Tokyo Metropolitan Government -- 23-ward and Greater Tokyo modal split, rail ~50% centrally), Singapore LTA Household Interview Travel Survey (HITS) 2023 (upper-mid density band: car ~20-25%, public transport ~45%, active mobility ~20%).
provenance.note: Band anchor values are hand-fitted to match the three cited surveys' headline splits at their respective density regimes, then smoothly extended across the 8 bands below by the authors of this table (not independently measured at every band). Treat as directional pending Aaron's balance pass; the ORDERING (car share falls monotonically with density, rail/metro share rises monotonically) is the load-bearing claim, not the exact percentages.

modeIdNote: walk/bicycle/car/motorbike/taxi/bus/tram/metro/heavy_rail/ferry key exactly to data/modes.json's 'id' field (reference, not restated). hs_rail is this table's own id, a density-varying SPLIT of modes.json's heavy_rail mode share into conventional-rail and high-speed-rail sub-markets -- see vehicle_classes.json's hs_rail row and link_capacity.json's hs1 class for the physical distinction.

bands.source: UK DfT National Travel Survey, rural settlement-type mode split (BUG-824: real-survey anchor #1 of 3)
hand-fitted interpolation between the rural (UK NTS) and low_urban anchors, not independently surveyed
hand-fitted interpolation between the small_town and dense_urban anchors, not independently surveyed
hand-fitted interpolation between the low_urban and dense_urban anchors, not independently surveyed
hand-fitted interpolation between the medium_urban and high_density (Singapore HITS) anchors, not independently surveyed
Singapore LTA Household Interview Travel Survey (HITS) 2023, upper-mid density planning area (car ~20-25%, public transport ~45%, active mobility ~20%) (BUG-824: real-survey anchor #2 of 3)

Tokyo Metropolitan Area Person Trip Survey (5th round, MLIT/Tokyo Metropolitan Government), central-ward rail share ~50% (tram+metro+heavy_rail+hs_rail here sums to 0.45, closest band to that figure) (BUG-824: real-survey anchor #3 of 3)
extrapolated beyond the metro_core (Tokyo PTS) anchor toward the brief's 98M/megacity extreme, not independently surveyed

interpolationRule: For a density strictly between two adjacent band thresholds, linearly interpolate each mode's share by density fraction t = (density - loThreshold) / (hiThreshold - loThreshold), then renormalise the 11-vector to sum exactly to 1.0 (floating-point drift correction only, never a substantive re-weighting). Below the lowest threshold, use the 'rural' band unchanged; at or above the highest threshold, use 'megacity' unchanged. See traffic-assumptions.md A-6.
